_comment: Which Bitwarden machine accounts this repository uses, and when each stops working.
NO SECRET IS IN THIS FILE. A BWS access token carries no expiry inside it -- expiry is
a property of the machine account, held server-side and visible only in the web vault.
So the date has to be written down by whoever minted the token.
`expires` HAS THREE STATES, and the difference matters:
a date  -- the account stops working then;
null    -- it never expires. This is Bitwarden's DEFAULT: the access-token docs say
"When the token Expires. By default, Never." The file modelled `expires`
as required until 2026-09-09 because the one token it described happened
to carry a 7-day life, which made the default look like the exception;
"unknown" -- nobody in this repository has verified it. NOT the same as null, and
writing null in its place would be a claim rather than a record.
THE POSTURE IS NOW THE SPLIT THIS FILE ANTICIPATED. It used to hold one row,
mc_migrate_claude, marked `used_by: [local, ci, cd]`, and the note below predicted a
split into a read-only account and a read-write one. That happened on 2026-09-09:
* local-rw-account   -- read-write, LOCAL ONLY, development and testing, never expires.
* ci-readonly-console -- read-only, what CI and CD use. Untouched by the rotation.
THE OLD ROW WAS DELETED, NOT EDITED. mc_migrate_claude expired 2026-09-08 and the
operator deleted the access token; a row describing a credential that no longer exists
is worse than no row. Its 2026-09-05 note claimed it was "the SOLE credential path for
CI and CD, so its expiry is a total outage" -- that was FALSE and was measured false on
2026-09-09: the local token was dead for at least a day while Autopilot run 34294177912
ran green, because CI was already on ci-readonly-console. A one-row file could not
represent that, which is why the claim survived unchallenged.
`client_id_sha256` fingerprints the IDENTIFIER half of the token -- the `<client-id>` of
`0.<client-id>.<secret>:<key>` -- never the secret. It exists so a token swapped without
updating this file is reported. It EARNED that on 2026-09-09: the live token digested to
26333295628e70e8 against a recorded 00991b3077ee8f57, which is how the swap was proven
rather than assumed.
`warn_days` is how long before a DATED expiry the tools start shouting. A row with null
or "unknown" is never warned about, because there is nothing to count down to.
NO CI GATE READS THIS. Settled deliberately (docs/ci-overhaul/08-driver-contract.md
sec 2): an expired token already fails loudly at every call site, and a clock-driven
gate reds the tree on a quiet day for a condition no commit caused. Re-examined
2026-09-09 after the outage above and the settlement HELD -- a fingerprint gate would
have been green throughout, since the fingerprint matched right up until the swap.
The one reader is scripts/ops/bws-map-refresh.py, which warns and continues.

tokens.name: local-rw-account
tokens.replacement_plan: None needed: it never expires. If it is ever rotated, update client_id_sha256 here in the same change -- the fingerprint is what makes a silent swap loud.

tokens.name: ci-readonly-console
tokens.replacement_plan: Not rotated on 2026-09-09 and not inspected. Its fingerprint and expiry are unknown to this repository because the token lives only in the GitHub secret BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN, which no session can read. Fill both in from the web vault when convenient; until then a swap of the CI credential cannot be detected here.
